subject: Manufacturing slot hedge & partial delivery terms for NimbusAI deal
messages:
From: Tara Lin <tara.lin@nebula-oem.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T09:02:00-07:00
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Manufacturing slot availability — proposal attached

Rafael,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a formal slot offer for a November manufacturing tranche plus an option window in Q1. Highlights:
- Firm allocation: 120 units (A100-class equivalent) shipping across 2 partial shipments (70 / 50)
- Hold fee (escrow): 15% refundable against initial invoice if Redwood converts within 90 days
- Priority lane: paid upgrade that moves orders ahead by 2 production slots (subject to OEM confirmation)
- Estimated lead-time: 14–18 weeks from PO receipt for first tranche, 10–14 for second tranche

See attached: nebula_oem_slot_offer_v2.pdf (pricing, payment milestones, cancellation terms).

If you want, we can convert the hold fee into a vendor credit that Redwood draws down against future orders — helps with customer-facing accounting.

Best,
Tara
Tara Lin
Head of Partnerships, Nebula OEM
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T10:18:00-07:00
To: Tara Lin <tara.lin@nebula-oem.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Manufacturing slot availability — proposal attached

Tara — thanks for the PDF. Quick read and a few clarifying asks so we can present a clean procurement ask to our finance/procure teams and to NimbusAI: 

1) Escrow mechanics: does the 15% hold fee require Redwood legal to sign Nebula terms, or can it sit in a neutral escrow (third-party) with a time-based release? Our procurement prefers third-party escrow for refundable holds.
2) Partial shipments: can Nebula guarantee continuity of firmware and QA across the two partial shipments (we need identical CVE patch levels and identical thermal profiles for identical batches)? If not, we need acceptance stanzas for batch variance.
3) Priority lane cap: if we opt for the paid priority upgrade, how many orders per quarter are guaranteed to move forward (we need a firm SLA, e.g., move ahead by X manufacturing slots or by Y weeks)?
4) Backfill plan: what cloud backfill can Nebula coordinate if manufacturing slips? We are trying to use CloudCorp reserved instances as a temporary backstop — if Nebula can confirm a refundable credit we can coordinate with CloudCorp for a blended solution.

Marissa — can you map expected onboarding windows vs the proposed shipments? Karthik — can you confirm if the 15% hold fee sits within our capital constraints for DEAL-8342? Ben — FYI on commercial option.

Short timeline: NimbusAI wants run-of-show confirmed by next Tuesday. Can we get a formal redline-ready slot confirmation by Friday?

Thanks,
Rafael
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Tara Lin <tara.lin@nebula-oem.com>
Date: 2027-09-24T11:07:00-07:00
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Manufacturing slot availability — proposal attached

Rafael, Marissa — quick answers inline: 

1) Escrow mechanics: Nebula can accept a third-party escrow (we typically use Locksafe Escrow). We will draft an escrow instruction that mirrors the 15% refundable hold and conditions for release on conversion/cancellation.

2) Partial shipments & QA parity: we confirm same firmware baseline across the tranche; we will include batch-level QA reports and a matching acceptance certificate for both shipments. Any deviation beyond the published tolerance triggers a remedy (repair/replace).

3) Priority lane SLA: we can guarantee movement ahead by 2 production slots or 3 weeks, whichever is shorter, and we will log priority upgrades on our scheduling portal for audit. SLA will be contractual via an addendum.

4) Backfill coordination: we cannot directly provision CloudCorp capacity but will provide a refundable credit against the hold fee that Redwood can apply to CloudCorp invoices for a 30-day backfill. We'll attach a short MOU for accounting flow.

I'll circulate an updated slot confirmation that replaces the generic hold instruction with third-party escrow language — expect that by EOD Thursday.

—Tara
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-25T09:30:00-07:00
To: Tara Lin <tara.lin@nebula-oem.com>, CloudCorp Sales <cloudsales@cloudcorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Subject: Fwd: Manufacturing slot availability — procurement constraints and backfill ask

Tara/CloudCorp — forwarding our internal constraints so you have the procurement lens. Short version: we can fund the 15% hold fee but need 1) neutral escrow instrument, 2) invoice milestone alignment with our committed revenue recognition dates, and 3) explicit interchange for vendor credit -> CloudCorp backfill.

CloudCorp — can you provide a short CSV of on-demand vs reserved backfill pricing for an A100-class pool, and an estimate of how quickly you can provision a 50-unit temporary pool for up to 60 days? Attach to reply if possible.

Note: finance will need the vendor credit flow documented before releasing PO. I'm copying Ben for commercial alignment, Marissa for onboarding window mapping.

Karthik
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference
From: CloudCorp Sales <cloudsales@cloudcorp.com>
Date: 2027-09-27T16:45:00-07:00
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tara Lin <tara.lin@nebula-oem.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Anuj Mehta <anuj@nimbusai.com>
Subject: Re: Manufacturing slot availability — procurement constraints and backfill ask

Karthik / team — attaching the requested backfill pricing and a provisional provisioning SLA. Key points: 
- 50-unit temporary pool (A100-class equiv) can be provisioned in 72–96 hours in us-west-2 for on-demand; reserved carveouts require a 7–10 day lead for dedicated reservation setup.
- On-demand blended rate: $XX/hr per unit (see cloud_backfill_pricing_v1.csv).
- We can accept a Nebula-issued vendor credit applied against CloudCorp invoices; finance will need the credit memo flow and a matching statement of work.

Action items: 1) Tara: confirm vendor-credit amount and mechanics so we can draft a credit memo template. 2) Redwood: if you want guaranteed 50-unit backfill for >30 days, we need signed SOW and a 7-day lead to finalize network / VPC peering.

Anuj (NimbusAI) — looping you so you see the available backfill cadence as we finalize the manufacturing tranche.

Thanks,
Samir Raghavan
Enterprise Sales, CloudCorp
